Global attack on Health care systems

By: Liz Fish | Commission

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
South Africa’s National Health Laboratory Service (NHLS) was hacked in a ransomware attack in late June, and doctors say it has thrown medical care back two decades to an era when computerised systems were still rudimentary by today’s standards. Global attacks on health care systems is on the rise, with 1163 facilities attack in Africa in the last year, and NHS and Irish health care systems have also been taken down taking months to rebuild and causing back logs in blood results of up to 6 months.

Thousands of operations have had to be cancelled in South Africa. Doctors cannot access their patients’ histories, or get results from tests or biopsies performed in the last few weeks - 6.3 million blood tests would have been conducted since the attack.
The knock-on effect is that hospitals which are already over-burdened are slowing down, unable to release patients because treatment is taking much longer. Outpatients have to keep returning to clinics because results are delayed. The fear is that critical illness will simply go untreated. As happened with Covid-19, the full extent will only be understood in six months’ time.


Summary:
The NHLS is an independent service which hospitals pay for, and the backbone of the health services. By shutting out the NHLS from its online system the hackers have denied 80% of the population access to their own medical records.
South Africa has become an easy target for hackers with a series of major hacks in the last few years. Spending and updating security is money the Health Department has been reluctant to spend.

Now although the labs are running, the tests have to be printed out and distributed on paper. Lab reports are normally automatically generated and sent to the doctors or made available on web view. But the hack has disabled this function. Doctors are spending hours on the phone trying to get urgent results – people simply cannot get through to the few phone lines that are being operated. If the laboratory is in the hospital, student doctors have to physically collect them – they say they are clocking up to 34km a day walking the corridors of a large hospital like Baragwanath.
NHLS was a prime target for hackers because the stakes are so high, and spending money on security systems has not been a priority within State services. And state institutions have a policy of not responding to hijack threats and made no contact with the hacker, “Black Suit”. A week after the hack on Saturday 22 June, the hackers’ middleman contacted medical journalist Chris Bateman trying to get the NHLS to pay the ransom. “Over one terabyte of data can be released – or deleted,” was the threat made.

Further information:
A cyber expert will give us the overview to how these hackers function- the rise in attacks on healthcare system and why South Africa is an increasing target for hackers.

Extra Budget Items:
I will need an extra half day to shoot recreations. The shoot is in East London as I have access there to the rural clinic and Cecelia Makiwane lab and hospital.

Script:


Sound from hacker
VO “A spine-chilling message” - pause - “with potentially fatal consequences”
Dominic “This is probably the first time a cyber-attack has led to the deaths, albeit indirectly, of South African citizens
VO “triggering an unprecedented crisis in our health system
Kolega “ I thought Covid was a nightmare, but this has been a completely different nightmare
Chris “ l got a call it was about 10 at night this guy with a very thick Eastern European accent, speaking very fast,
VO: “Weeks later critical elements of public and private healthcare are still on their knees, with no corner left untouched.”
VO: Dr Jenny Nash Eastern Cape district clinician leaves early for her monthly visit to the rural clinics
Jenny “ When I got to the clinic last time I was sort of wondering why we couldn't access all our results- it was only then that I started to realise the sort of implications”
VO: Visiting every month for the last 18 years she has weathered many health crises.They rely heavily on the extremely efficient online National Health Laboratory Service- to provide healthcare for this community of over 10 000 people
Upsound from Jenny examining the baby asking for for the nurse to look for the paper result
VO: Normally able to access patient history and pathology results on their phones and computers - they have been working in a vacuum since a cyber attack targeting the country's critical lab services six weeks ago.
Jenny “ ja, that was done in June, there is no result, so these are the ones I would look at and decide whether I was going to continue the treatment or adjust the treatment, …
VO: These patients have been here since 7 in the morning. From here, they'll be sent to a hospital or have their treatment adjusted. But it's a process now made infinitely more complicated by faceless computer hackers."
Jenny “ So now I have looked at the folders waiting for me it means that you even have to just go on clinical suspicion.
breather
VO In other words a plot hatched by random cybercriminals somewhere in the world, forced clinicians to make unreliable diagnosis - sabotaging public health
breather
LINK: Cyber criminals have no morals or boundaries hacking indiscriminately, singling out health care among the top three targets worldwide
VO: It's hard to conceive criminals would attack a healthcare system - demanding outrageous ransoms - knowing lives are at stake.
Breather
upsound from hacker voice
"A recording that left Koleka Mlisana cold. She'd been in the job as CEO of the National Health Laboratory Service for just over a month."
Erin: Some people have said that NHLS is like the backbone of public healthcare. How would you describe it?
Kolega “ Every clinical decision that is made, about 70 to 80% of those decisions rely on pathology., we provide our services to more than 80% of the population of the country. And how many samples do.we process a month, around 12, 13 million a month.
VO Calling themselves Blacksuit, the hackers froze the Lab Service on the 22nd of June this year."
Kolega everybody just got shut out, we could not access emails, people could not access our systems, and it meant the labs could not operate.
UPSOUND of Dominic at the laptop with Erin showing where Blacksuit comes from
VO: Cyber security expert Dominic White says little is known about Blacksuit
Upsound
Dom: What happens with these ransomware gangs is they get arrested, they have fallen out, people get sanctioned, so they split up and splinter. Sometimes they rebrand just because there's bad things associated with the previous name
VO: Dominic heads up a global cyber security company - helping to shore up the defences against the increasingly sophisticated cyber attacks
Dominic:, they only notify the client …..and exert that extortion pressure after they've completed the hack. ….They've managed to understand and map out the organization, ransack all of the data, whether they're deleting or encrypting it
VO It is at this point the ghastly message appears - providing a link to begin negotiations
Kolega “ there was a link included in their communication which the IT people could actually see on the system but then we were advised don't you dare touch that link because you don't know the implications. From the NHLS perspective we did not open that link whatsoever.
VO: Refusing to negotiate they have no idea what ransom Blacksuit was demanding
Kolega” The cyber security specialists have come on board. CSIR has been assisting us and we also had a First Rand Bank you know, assisting us pro bono.
VO: As the NHLS scrambled for solutions and with negotiations a non-starter, events took a strange turn. Apparently frustrated by the lack of communication, the attackers made a call out of the blue, dragging a local medical journalist into the fray.
Until then, Chris Bateman had merely reported on the hack
Chris “ It was about just after ten one night, and I got a call…… this guy with a very thick Eastern European accent, ….he said, I want you to give a message to the NHLS leadership, Kolega Milisana and we can fix this in a couple of hours
CHRIS reading the link back to them
VO: Ransomware attacks are increasingly complex. It's a lucrative business projected to cost the world 10 trillion dollars
Breather
VO: In 2017 ransomware called “Wannacry” hit The National Health System in the United Kingdom causing havoc- and costing over 92 million pounds.
It was attacked again in 2022 costing 40 million pounds.
Breather
LINK Clip 160 Bizarrely the crimes of a gang of hackers on the other side of the world is being felt here at a rural Eastern Cape Clinic
Erin “ Normally you open up your phone and you can track a timeline for a patient in terms of their bloods over time, at it is all at the touch of a fingertip and suddenly you are just locked out
Jenny: a huge frustration where you have a patient who comes in and they might have been seen in another province and the tracklab allowed you to go back and gave you the perspective of this patient so suddenly isnt almost 2 D sitting in front of you they almost 3D they have got dimension so you have just got that background of the patient
VO: Doctors are describing it as the biggest single disaster to have hit the public health sector..
Breather
VO: Online results are critical in hospitals . But results have to be physically collected from the labs and in chronically understaffed hospitals- it can be 3 to 4 days to reach the ward.
VO: Operations have been postponed and patients left hanging for answers.
Jenny “ I think it probably affects junior doctors more……perhaps they haven't faced lots of challenges over many years and perhaps don't have as much confidence clinically. That can be very, terrifying. You don't you don't have results coming back to you
Upsound Babonke” that one is done outside of East London so I will need to take your details and call you back”
VO: Young doctors like Salomay Kotze are desperate
Salomay:.we are chasing, like, urgent results in influencing patients management. Um, I mean, we are feeding and supplementing patients by giving IV fluids and giving treatments and not always sure what we are actually doing if we're doing more harm than good. I've been phoning since yesterday for some results and I've not even been able to get hold of some of the laboratories
VO: The Cecelia Makiwane laboratory runs 13 000 tests a month. Over and above the hospital, they service 19 facilities from the surrounding area.
Breather
LINK Clip 214/215 Having run a state of the art laboratory service they have been reduced to doing things manually and its taking double the time to get results out
Upsound
VO: Laboratory manager Babonke Zoleka is exhausted, his staff are torn between processing specimens and communicating urgent results to clinicians.
Babonke: Previously you would have just to load the instrument, it would scan all the tests that are requested. But now you have to select each and every test that is requested on the instrument to tell it what test must be processed.
Upsound of shuffling papers
VO: Even if the NHLS had paid the ransom - there were no guarantees the hackers would restore the data.
Taking six weeks to secure the system it slowly come back online
Erin: doctors in some cases feel that you didn't do enough, that you didn't set up a hotline exclusively to deal with the results, that you weren't strategic enough with your use of WhatsApp and other alternative technologies,
Kolega “ I will accept it if clinicians feel we could have communicated better. ….Unfortunately, there is no direct access to clinicians in the public sector.But we really tried to do media released to all the various whatsapp groups that are there for the time being “
So - did the NHLS do enough to protect this critical service?
Dominic. So a lot of the time people rush to blame the victims ….There's no evidence that the NHLS was negligent here. …the hackers were possibly just innovative would like that to be a bit of a rallying cry with, with the South African government to embolden our efforts to work with international law enforcement, to target these gangs, and to put a lot more effort into securing our parastatals or SOEs and and direct government institutions.
VO: after 6 weeks pathology results came back online and patient data before the hack restored - after that it remains a black hole
Erin: if you could, uh, speak to the hackers … what would you say to them?
Salomay: Laugh, I would almost get emotional - no, I feel like it's evil.
